speechtext: Mr. Chairman, it appears to me that the number of people participating in a pool is left wide open. Is there any minimum size or maximum size, or is it just a wide open affair?

speakerposition: Minister of Transport; Minister responsible for the Canadian Wheat Board
subsubtopic: MEASURE RESPECTING ESTABLISHMENT OF MARKETING PLANS
speechtext: That is not spelled out. In that sense it is wide open. A certain number would have to be sought for administrative viability, so the proposers no doubt will have that in mind. The maximum number would result from the Financial security which has to be posted.

subsubtopic: MEASURE RESPECTING ESTABLISHMENT OF MARKETING PLANS
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, page 3 of the bill deals with the establishment of marketing plans. Reference is made to an association representing a signiFicant number of producers. Then later on it refers to making an order if there are a sufFicient number of producers. I am wondering what is the difference between "a significant number" and "a sufFicient number" and why the same words are not used. There must be some distinction.

speakerposition: Minister of Transport; Minister responsible for the Canadian Wheat Board
subsubtopic: MEASURE RESPECTING ESTABLISHMENT OF MARKETING PLANS
speechtext: Mr. Chairman, would the hon. member please draw my attention to the word "sufficient"?

subsubtopic: MEASURE RESPECTING ESTABLISHMENT OF MARKETING PLANS
speechtext: On page 3, clause 35.11(1) says: "Any association representing a signiFicant number of producers engaged in the production of grain ..." Clause 35.12 makes reference to a sufFicient number. Then on page 4 the bill refers to a signiFicant number again.

speakerposition: Minister of Transport; Minister responsible for the Canadian Wheat Board
subsubtopic: MEASURE RESPECTING ESTABLISHMENT OF MARKETING PLANS
speechtext: A significant number would be a judgment on the part of the association as to whether it has that kind of support, when it is an association and not a company which is proposing a plan. A sufficient number again would be a judgment. It may not be different from a signiFicant number, but I think it would be many fewer. It may be those who are actually participating, willing to participate, and therefore sufFicient to make a plan worthwhile. It is that non-minimum which is, however, meant to be judged by the governor in council as being enough.

subsubtopic: MEASURE RESPECTING ESTABLISHMENT OF MARKETING PLANS
speechtext:
Mr. Chairman, further to the minister's reply to the hon. member for Moose Jaw, I take it that in the first instance there must be what appears to be a significant number and an appropriate association, in the view of the

June 13, 1977
Canadian Wheat Board Act
minister, to go into a voluntary plan, on the one hand; and then in the course of a sign-up it would be a matter of judgment for the minister as to whether, even though the association represents a significant number, there is a sufficient number to make the plan work, and that this lies in the hands of the minister.

speakerposition: Minister of Transport; Minister responsible for the Canadian Wheat Board
subsubtopic: MEASURE RESPECTING ESTABLISHMENT OF MARKETING PLANS
speechtext: That is correct.

subsubtopic: MEASURE RESPECTING ESTABLISHMENT OF MARKETING PLANS
speechtext: I am still referring to clause 35.12 and to the explanation just given by the minister concerning a sufficient number of producers. Will the regulations determine in greater detail the meaning of producers? What will influence the minister's decision: the volume of grain or the number of producers?

speakerposition: Minister of Transport; Minister responsible for the Canadian Wheat Board
subsubtopic: MEASURE RESPECTING ESTABLISHMENT OF MARKETING PLANS
speechtext: We are really looking here at the number of producers. I do not see a practical problem because the administrators of a plan would not want to go forward with it unless they had a fairly large volume of grain and producers. Therefore, we would not have much difficulty with making a judgment.
